sentences.text: Avimimus was a small, bird-like dinosaur measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length and standing 45 centimeters tall at the hip.
It possessed a small skull relative to its body, yet it had a large brain and enormous eye sockets protected by large bones.
Instead of teeth, the animal had a horny beak very similar to that of parrots, with tooth-like projections found at the tip of the premaxilla.
Avimimus was officially described by Dr. Sergei Kurzanov in 1981 after being recovered by Russian paleontologists.
A new species, Avimimus nemegtensis, was formally described in 2018 based on previously identified material.
The preservation of bonebeds suggests the animals were buried quickly by a rapid water flow and then reburied a short distance away.
While Kurzanov hypothesized it was an insectivore, it is debated whether Avimimus was an herbivore or omnivore given the toothless beak.
Recent studies group Avimimus within the family Oviraptoridae and the parent group Oviraptorosauria.
It coexisted with dinosaurs such as the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus and the hadrosaurid Saurolophus in the Nemegt Formation.
It is debated whether Avimimus originated from the Djadokhta Formation as originally thought, with evidence suggesting it likely hailed from the more recent Nemegt Formation.
